chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Hafs, from Saeed ibn Yasar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: One evening, while we were in Mina, he was encouraging me regarding the Hajj and making me desirous of it.

O Saeed! Whichever servant is granted sustenance by Allah from His sustenance, so he takes that sustenance and spends it upon himself and his dependents. Then he takes them out, having exposed them to the sun, until he brings them to the evening of Arafat to the Standing Place.
He says: Do you not see a relief (open spot) there, with a gap in it, and no one in it? So I said: Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.
So he says: He comes with them, having exposed them, until he fills that relief with them.

Then Allah, Blessed and High, the One with no partner, says: My servant, I granted him from My sustenance, so he took that sustenance and spent it, exposing himself and his dependents by it. Then he came with them until he filled with them this relief, seeking My forgiveness.
I forgive his sin, and suffice him for whatever worries him, and provide for him.
Saeed said: Along with the things which he said, there were approximately ten.

key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: Arafat (the place of standing during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for spending on one's family during Hajj according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the profound merit of *Duhā* (exposure to the sun) during Hajj, framing it as an active pursuit of divine forgiveness. The narration emphasizes that spending one's God-given sustenance on oneself and family, followed by enduring the physical hardship of standing at Arafat, serves as a comprehensive act of worship that secures Allah's protection from worldly anxieties and ensures provision.
